annotation.title_clean: Council Directive 89/392/EEC of 14 June 1989 on the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to machinery
annotation.title_en: Council Directive 89/392/EEC of 14 June 1989 on the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to machinery
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Communities L 183 (EUR-Lex)
annotation.summary_en: The original 1989 EEC Machinery Directive harmonises member-state laws on machinery safety. It sets essential health and safety requirements, conformity declaration, EC marking, type-examination by notified bodies, and reliance on harmonised standards. It is a foundational legal basis for later robot and industrial machine safety regulation, without AI content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Machinery may be placed on the market only if it does not endanger health or safety of persons
Machinery must meet essential health and safety requirements in Annex I, including control system safety and emergency stops
Manufacturers issue EC declaration of conformity and affix EC mark; Annex IV machines need notified body type-examination
Conformity with harmonised standards (CEN/Cenelec) creates presumption of conformity
Safeguard clause lets Member States withdraw unsafe CE-marked machinery with Commission consultation
